text: Light brown pigmentation in the epidermal layer indicates melanin production.
Blue-gray pigmentation in the dermal layer indicates hyperpigmentation.
Deep creases, wrinkles, and loss of skin laxity characterize an extremely coarse skin texture.
Deep nasolabial folds and marionette grooves are visible signs of aging.
Thin and lax skin on the neck indicates advanced age or skin laxity.
Marionette grooves are folds extending from the corners of the mouth downwards.
Crepelike skin texture in the periorbital region indicates skin laxity or aging.
Platysmal bands are visible lines or ridges on the neck, which may appear asymmetric or prominent during animation.
Brow ptosis is characterized by a drooping or lowered position of the eyebrow.
Thinning skin and loss of elasticity lead to the presence of rhytides (wrinkles).
The formation of jowls and the deepening of marionette lines signal facial aging.
Facial lines, irregular pigmentation, telangiectasias, and textural changes serve as visible indicators of aging and photodamage.
Dyschromias and irregular pigmentation indicate sun damage or skin discoloration.
Scarring or textural irregularities can be present on the skin surface.
Fine, clear, almost invisible vellus hair is seen on the forehead.
A receding hairline with thinning at the top of the head while preserving hair in the temporal and occipital areas signals male pattern baldness.
Loss of eyebrows or eyelashes can indicate trauma, burns, or surgical excision.
Depict male pattern baldness starting at the anterior hairline and advancing in a posterior direction without a peninsula of hair.
condition: when describing a specific variant of male pattern baldness

text: Depict female androgenic alopecia as generalized thinning that spares the front hairline but shows significant thinning at the vertex, temple, and parietal areas.
Loss of eyebrows and scalp hair can indicate posttraumatic alopecia from injuries like burns or scalp avulsion.
The absence of mustache hair can be a sign of a bilateral cleft lip.
condition: in the context of congenital hair loss

text: Depict a hairline with a slight frontotemporal recession to create a natural look consistent with a mature age.
condition: when designing a portrait of a mature man

text: For a man with severe hair loss (type VII), focus hair density on the median forelock area to frame the face while leaving the crown bare.
condition: when depicting extreme male pattern baldness

text: Depict uniform thinning over the entire scalp while preserving the front hairline for a woman with Ludwig grade II to III alopecia.
Coarse or wavy hair texture provides more visual coverage for thinning areas than fine hair.
A pattern of male pattern baldness type VII represents the most severe form of hair loss.
Uniform thinning over the entire scalp with a preserved front hairline is characteristic of Ludwig grade II to III female androgenic alopecia.
Male pattern baldness type III is characterized by vertex hair loss without frontotemporal recession.
Hair fullness is visually communicated through hair mass, which is determined by the number of hairs, individual shaft thickness, texture, color, and curliness.
Excess skin on the upper eyelid is a sign of periorbital aging.
Ptosis (drooping) of the brow and eyelid complex signals early signs of aging.
The loss of the lateral scleral triangle signals increasing lid laxity and age.
Scleral show, where the white of the eye is visible below the iris, indicates lid laxity and aging.
A higher eyelid crease gives the impression of having less skin.
Asian orbits tend to be more round, whereas Caucasian orbits tend to be more square with a prominent superior orbital rim and deeper lateral orbital rim.
The epicanthal fold (epicanthus tarsalis) is a fold from the upper lid to the medial canthus.
Asian eyelids often lack a lid crease due to the point of fusion between the septum orbicularis and dermis.
An Asian upper eyelid crease, when present, is approximately 6 to 8 mm from the lid margin.
A tapered eyelid crease gradually converges to blend in with the medial epicanthal fold.
A parallel eyelid crease remains parallel medially and stays above the epicanthal fold.
The presence of fat prolapse combined with superior sulcus hollowing is a visible sign of aging in Asian eyelids.
Excessive scleral show, where the white of the eye is overly visible, can make the eye appear too large.
Advanced sun-damaged skin can be used to characterize an elderly or aged appearance.
An implosion-like appearance is caused by volume loss or deflation in the face.
Represent facial sagging as a downward movement at the periphery of the face and the neck.
A lengthening or descending vertical height of the upper lip is a sign of facial aging.
The appearance of perioral rhytids (barcode wrinkles) and an accentuated nasolabial crease signals facial aging.
A lengthened vertical distance between the alar base and the vermiliocutaneous border indicates aging of the upper lip.
The oral commissures of a young person are horizontal or curve slightly upward.
Aging is signaled by a loss of definition in the vermiliocutaneous border, a fading Cupid’s bow, and the appearance of vertical rhytids on the skin surface.
Downward-turning oral commissures and a loss of philtral column prominence indicate an aged appearance.
Visible fat lobules under the lower eyelid skin indicate superficial fat deposition.
condition: in a portrait showing the lower eyelid area

text: Depict a transverse nasal crease that runs perpendicular to the procerus muscle.
Depict the nasojugal crease at the lid-cheek junction.
Ensure the lower lip shows significantly more vermilion than the upper lip.
The upper lip should be approximately two-thirds the size of the lower lip.
Drooping of the tail of the eyebrow and fine wrinkles in the frontal and glabellar areas signal advanced age.
Loss of definition in the jowl line and the presence of platysmal bands on the neck signal aging and skin laxity.
Deep creases and skin folds below the cricoid cartilage indicate poor cervical skin elasticity.
A smooth volumetric blending between the eyelid and the cheek indicates a youthful appearance.
condition: when the lateral component of deep malar fat abuts the orbit and SOOF

text: Volumetric highlights on the malar pad and zygomatic eminence indicate a youthful face.
The presence of facial jowls caused by descending soft tissue in the lower cheek indicates aging.
A bottom-heavy square facial shape with little difference between malar highlights and midfacial fat signals middle age.
An angular, tapered facial appearance characterized by fullness in the malar region and a concavity over the buccal recess signals youth.
Demarcation lines between adjacent regions of the cheek signal middle age due to deflation and radial expansion.
Depict the face with well-supported fat overlying the malar eminence and lateral cheek.
Depict the face with a square shape and increased fullness in the jowl and submalar region.
Submalar concavity and deflation in the lateral and middle compartments signal facial aging.
A loss of the angular, tapered shape of youth and a reduction in malar volume signal aging.
Increased malar volume and bizygomatic diameter make a face appear wider.
Depict aging through three categories: skin surface breakdown (wrinkles, age spots), facial sagging/loss of contour, and facial wasting or atrophy.
Hollowing and flattening of the midface area, combined with a loss of the smooth transition between the lower eyelid and cheek, signals an elderly appearance.
Atrophy in the cheeks and infraorbital areas suggests an older appearance.
Hollowness in the upper and lower eyelid areas and cheek sag can signal a tired or aged appearance.
Deep creases from strong frown muscles and a downward mouth position signal a stern and disapproving appearance.
Hooded upper eyelids, sagging cheeks, and deep cheek folds signal a tired and disinterested appearance.
Hollow upper eyelids and sagging cheeks can signal a sad appearance even when the subject is smiling.
Sagging cheeks, heavy jowls, and thin lips can signal a stern and disapproving appearance.
Sagging cheeks, deep cheek folds, and jowls signal facial volume loss and aging.
Panfacial atrophy and cheek laxity signal a fragile, haggard, or ill appearance.
condition: in elderly subjects with significant tissue loss

text: Long, narrow eyes are characteristic of young people with normal periorbital morphology.
Scleral show (visible white of the eye below the iris) is associated with a negative vector relationship where the globe lies ahead of the midface soft tissues.
A 'skin on muscle' appearance where platysma bands are clearly visible along their entire course signals a lack of preplatysmal fat.
A full, obtuse, and lumpy neck appearance is characteristic of patients with large submandibular glands or significant subplatysmal fat.
Sagging tissue and loss of contour in the submental area (under the chin) signals an aged or degraded appearance.
condition: when describing or judging the neck area

text: Dimpling and irregularity of the chin can be a visible skin feature.
Eyelid laxity and dermatochalasis (excess skin on eyelids) are visible signs of advanced age.
A lengthened upper lip that covers the upper incisors like a curtain signals advanced aging.
A thin, deflated vermilion and the lower lip falling into the mouth creates a gaunt and ill appearance.
A male face is characterized by a wider, squarer jawline and a two-point light reflection on the chin.
Depict men with wider, squarer faces and more projected chins.
The male nasal dorsal profile should hug a line drawn from the radix to the tip-defining points.
The male nasal tip should be broader and more bulbous.
The nose of a person of African heritage typically features a wide, low nasal dorsum, decreased nasal length and tip projection, and alar flaring.
A Middle Eastern nose features thick, sebaceous skin and is most prominent at the supratip.
A Middle Eastern nose may feature a wide bony and middle vault and a significant dorsal hump.
Noses of African heritage typically feature a wide, low nasal dorsum, decreased nasal length and tip projection, less well defined nasal tip, an acute nasolabial angle, and alar flaring.
A droopy nasal tip is associated with an acute nasolabial angle.
A thick, sebaceous skin texture on the nasal tip and alar area is a characteristic feature of a Middle Eastern nose.
Thick, sebaceous, and inelastic skin on the nasal tip results in a poorly defined, flattened, and bulbous appearance.
A prominent supraorbital bossing and thick supraorbital ridge conveys masculinity.
Prominent malar eminences (cheekbones) convey femininity.
A shorter distance from the nasal base to the vermilion border conveys femininity.
A prominent thyroid cartilage with an acute angle at the laryngeal prominence conveys masculinity.
